subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the volume of the tetrahedron whose vertices are (1,2,1), (3,2,5), (2,−1,0) and (−1,0,1).

mark_split.label: Find the three edge vectors from A
Divide by 6 and state the volume

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.64 — SAQ chapter 9 Product of Vectors, answer 61. Printed appearances: TS 15,20. The difference from answer 60 is that VERTICES are given, not edges — so three subtractions come first. The book notes "Tetra means 4", which is the count of vertices, not of edges.THE MARK SPLIT IS PRINTED in that book's margin as [1 Mark] on the edge vectors, [2 Marks] on the determinant and [1 Mark] on the volume — a sourced 1+2+1 — a sourced split, not an inference. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q13 is the Product of Vectors slot.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the volume of a tetrahedron from its four vertices.

steps.label: Find the three edges
steps.margin_note: First mark. Four vertices, but only THREE edges are needed — all from the same corner A. That is what turns vertices into the form the formula wants.
steps.memory_tip: Four vertices but only THREE edges are needed, all from the same corner A.

recall.must_convey: That three edge vectors AB, AC and AD are built from the same vertex A by subtracting OA.
accept: find AB AC and AD all from the same vertex A by subtracting OA
three edges from one corner, not all six edges
subtract OA from the other three position vectors
A nunchi moodu edges AB AC AD teeskovali
build the three edge vectors from one vertex

steps.why: A tetrahedron has six edges, but three from one corner already determine it. Any other three would not span the solid.
common_mistakes: Missing a zero component — AB has no j term and AD has no k term.

steps.label: Evaluate the triple product
steps.margin_note: Half the marks, and the book prints [2 Marks] here. The zeros make two of the three expansion terms cheap — expand along the top row and use them.
steps.memory_tip: The zeros make two expansion terms cheap — expand along the top row and use them.

recall.must_convey: That the three edges form a determinant which evaluates to −36.
accept: the determinant of the three edges comes to minus thirty six
expand the triple product to get minus thirty six
the box product is minus thirty six
determinant expand cheste minus thirty six vasthundi
evaluate the scalar triple product, minus thirty six

steps.why: A negative triple product just means the three edges are ordered the other way round. The modulus in the formula removes that, which is why a volume is still positive.
common_mistakes: Assuming the negative determinant is a mistake and re-doing correct arithmetic.
Forgetting the middle term is multiplied by 0 and still writing it out.

steps.label: Divide by 6
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The modulus turns −36 into 36, and a sixth of that is 6. Cubic units.
steps.memory_tip: The modulus turns −36 into 36, and a sixth of that is 6. Cubic units.

recall.must_convey: That the modulus of −36 divided by 6 gives a volume of 6 cubic units.
accept: mod of minus thirty six over six is six cubic units
the volume is six cubic units
thirty six by six equals six
minus thirty six mod teesi six tho divide cheste six
the answer is six cubic units

steps.why: The modulus is doing real work here — without it the answer would be −6, which is not a volume.

insider_note: Vertices are given, not edges, so subtract first to get AB, AC and AD all starting at A. The modulus matters: −36 gives a volume of 6, never −6.
